column1: # Files malware leaves on disk. One line each, tab separated. After editing, run: bash tools/gen.sh
#   incident  an id from data/incidents.tsv
#   os        all, mac, linux or win (win is Git Bash and gird-check.ps1)
#   kind      wiper    a file of gh-token-monitor (its path must name it), the wiper that runs a destructive command when a
#                      stolen GitHub token is revoked. Section 5 tells people to stop it first.
#             startup  a file that starts malware at login; the note is shown under it
#             site     a file in any Python environment's site-packages: a Python incident's hit
#             temp     an entry in /tmp, TMPDIR or %TEMP%: a Python incident's hit. May end in *
#   owner     yes: counts only if this person owns it (for files in the shared /tmp; %TEMP% on Windows is the
#             person's own folder, so there it always counts). no otherwise
#   path      wiper and startup: a file or folder, with the path tokens data/sessions.tsv uses, an
#             absolute path, or {PROGRAMDATA} (Windows' ProgramData). site and temp: a file name
#   note      startup: what the file does, as shown under it. temp: what to do about the files, from the
#             incident's advisory, shown under the incident's row when they are found (the temp lines of one
#             incident carry the same note). - for wiper and site
# gh-token-monitor: Wiz (TanStack wave: the LaunchAgent and the systemd unit) and Socket (keyv wave: all six).
# Mastra: Socket. mistralai: its advisory, which lists the file and a process started through it as signs.
# LiteLLM: its advisory, and the GitHub issue the advisory links for the attack's details
# (BerriAI/litellm#47826), which names the .pc_ temp files and PRIVCOLLECT_ACTIVE: the .pc_once_ marker is
# written only once the data was sent, the advisory's "the exfil is confirmed".
# GlassWorm's LaunchAgent: Socket. A startup file of an incident whose packages are only editor
# extensions (data/bad-extensions.tsv) is shown with them, as that incident's sign, not as npm malware,
# and only when an extension that shipped malware is found: alone, it is a file to check.
